findings.summary: On long-form pages the lead stage is narrower than the prose column under it. It ends about 100px short of the text's right edge, while the in-article figure stage further down does span the full column. The spec says the lead image or drawing 'spans the text column'. The gap is small, but it leaves the lead looking unaligned with the text below.

The key-ring plate is a large open ring with a long leather strap and a tiny key hanging off it. At card size it reads first as a magnifying glass, and the key is the smallest part. This is the misread the recipe's step 5 warns about ('an object drawn without its defining part read as another'). The reference's small objects read at once.
In the stacked invoice list at 390px, each status badge stretches to the full width of the value column, so 'Due' and 'Paid' read as bars. On desktop the same badges hug their text.

One article section heading ('Lead with the / effect, not the cause') breaks onto two lines inside a wide column, with a short first line, while the other h2s on the page sit on one line. It looks like a narrow max-width or balance setting on that heading, and it breaks the steady rhythm of the section heads.

notes: Update goal (rc.3: every card grid of subject items gets a plate, even when the data has no image field). Reached in this sample. The blog home grid has a plate on all six post cards, each with its own drawing in its own color. The 'Related posts' grids have plates too, and each post's plate matches its lead stage on the detail page (the scroll is peach on the card and on the lead; the stamp is lilac on the featured stage and on its related card). The store grid has a plate on all 11 items. Link, resource and settings lists stay text-only. The rc.2 major is fixed.

Compared with the published 1.0.0: nothing got worse. The listing plates are back as 1.0.0 had them. The rc.2 fixes still hold: information figures are ghosted previews shaped like their captions (two panels for the release comparison, tiles for the inventory board), and the four metric cards sit 2x2 at 390px (dashboard home-mobile-light).

Earlier verdict (rc.2 critic-1). Its only major (lost listing plates) is fixed. Its two minors recur and are not re-raised: the sweater plate still reads as a slab held from below (commerce products-merino-crew-sweater-desktop-light), and the inventory-board preview is still one short row in a tall stage (blog posts-shipping-a-design-system-desktop-light).

Measured layout defect, false alarm: repeated-drawing on blog /posts/release-notes-people-read (desktop and mobile). The repeated SVG is svg.stage-lines, the faint wandering-line texture drawn on every stage (here the lead stage and the comparison figure stage). It is a background texture, not an illustration shown twice. The spec puts it on every stage, and the two subject drawings on the page are different.

Harness capture artifact, not counted: the dialog scrim ends at 900px in the full-page capture (settings state-plan-dialog-desktop-light). The dialog itself is designed: serif title, one line of consequence, Cancel and Confirm.
Gates: all passed on all four apps. The smoke tests were not run for this screen; they run at the confirm step.

Reference fidelity 4. Cream paper and warm ink, a serif display over a quiet sans, pastel stages with faint wandering lines, ink-black primary buttons, and generous section spacing. Compared with reference p1-desktop-light (plan cards with a small line drawing above a serif name, black primary buttons) and p3-desktop-light (calm stacked sections, small drawings over headings). Nothing is copied.

Signature 4. Drawings are present in all four apps: a header drawing beside every product h1, plates on every subject card, a drawing stage for the featured item and each lead, ghosted previews for figures, the primary chart on a sage stage, and plan cards on a stage. The hero hand-and-book steps in cel by cel and holds (blog motion-m1). Hands come from different edges in different poses. Held below 5 by the recurring weak drawings (sweater, key ring).

Component states 4: clay focus rings, danger-ringed fields with inline messages and a '3 fields need attention' line (commerce state-checkout-errors), filtered-empty states with a drawing, a title naming the filter and one clear action (dashboard state-empty-filter, blog state-search-empty), and a designed dialog. Cross-app 4: one family in light and dark (commerce home-mobile-dark, settings-profile-desktop-dark). Hierarchy 4: serif h1 with a drawing, then one stage or main card per screen. Polish 4: no browser-default leftovers apart from the minors listed.
